results.title: The Cheapest H100 Is Out of Stock: What 25 Clouds of GPU Pricing Data Shows | beCloudReady
results.author: Chandan Kumar
highlights:
October 13, 2026 6 min read

We track hourly GPU prices across 25 clouds every night. The cheapest H100 on our list is out of stock, and most providers do not publish stock at all. Here is what the data shows and how we handle it.

On 14 October 2026 the lowest H100 price in our tracker was $1.66 per GPU-hour, listed by Latitude. That row is marked out of stock. The cheapest H100 that a provider says you can rent right now is $3.30 per GPU-hour, at Scaleway. That is almost double.

...

After this week's changes, the 14 October snapshot has:

- 518 priced offers across 25 providers (up from 436 offers and 18 providers before the change)
- Hyperscalers (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Oracle) and GPU-specialist clouds in the same table
- A per-GPU-hour price, so an 8-GPU node and a single-GPU instance compare fairly

The jump in coverage came from one fix. Our marketplace source, Shadeform, can return every offer or only the ones with stock. We were asking for in-stock offers only, which hid seven providers whose capacity was exhausted at the time: Latitude, IMWT, DigitalOcean, BoostRun, Voltage Park, Horizon and Phyntec. We now keep those rows and label them.

## The new Availability column

Every row now carries an availability value:

- In stock: the provider reports capacity in at least one region. The price shown is the cheapest in-stock region, so it is a price you can rent.
- Out of stock: listed, but no region reports capacity. The price shown is the cheapest listed region.
- A dash: the provider does not publish stock, so we do not know.

The third case matters most. Stock data comes from the marketplace source only. AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Oracle, RunPod, Lambda, Nebius and the other direct sources publish prices but no stock. Of 518 offers, 51 are in stock, 158 are out of stock and 309 are unknown. We do not guess for those rows.

## What the data shows on 14 October

Median per-GPU-hour price of the offers in the tracker (not matched by instance size, so read these as a market snapshot rather than a benchmark):

| GPU | Offers | Providers | Lowest listed | Median | Highest listed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | 50 | 17 | $1.66 (Latitude, out of stock) | $3.25 | $10.00 (Oracle) |
| H200 | 21 | 10 | $2.25 (Excess Supply, out of stock) | $5.29 | $10.60 (Azure) |
| B200 | 17 | 9 | $3.74 (BoostRun, out of stock) | $7.79 | $14.24 (AWS) |
| A100 80GB | 45 | 14 | $1.35 (Excess Supply, in stock) | $1.98 | $4.10 (Azure) |
| L40S | 46 | 12 | $0.69 (BoostRun, out of stock) | $1.70 | $7.58 (AWS) |

Three things stand out.

1. The cheapest listing is usually not rentable. For H100, H200, B200 and L40S the lowest listed price is marked out of stock. For H100, 27 of the 50 offers are out of stock, 3 are in stock and 20 are unknown. A ranking that ignores this tells you to go to a provider that has nothing to sell you.

...

- On-demand only. ... They can change the ranking.
- Stock changes within hours. The snapshot is nightly. Treat it as where to look first, not as a reservation.
- Per-GPU price is not total cost. Egress, storage, minimum commitments and setup time are not in the number.

...

Data: public provider pricing APIs and catalogs, snapshot of 14 October 2026. Prices are USD per GPU-hour, on-demand.

results.title: GPU Dedicated Server Hosting: Monthly vs Hourly Math
results.author: Dmitry Schulz
highlights:
# GPU Dedicated Server Hosting: What a Monthly Commitment Actually Buys

Author:

Dmitry Schulz

October 8, 2026

Latitude.sh prices a bare-metal NVIDIA H100 80 GB at $1.68 an hour or $1,230 a month. Multiply the hourly rate by the 730 hours in an average month and you get $1,226.40 — the monthly plan costs $3.60 more than running the same server by the hour all month. Cherry Servers, meanwhile, takes about 19% off an A40 if you commit to the month.

Both are honest rate cards, and the difference between them is the most useful thing to understand before you sign for GPU capacity: the higher you go up the GPU range, the less a commitment buys you in price — and the more it buys you in access. This piece works through the published numbers and what they mean in practice.

## What a GPU dedicated server costs, from published rate cards

Every figure below comes from the provider’s own public page, read on 5 October 2026; the Latitude.sh, Hetzner and OVHcloud figures were re-checked on 7 October 2026. Currencies are as published, Hetzner prices exclude VAT, and no FX has been applied. “Break-even hours” is the monthly price divided by the hourly price — the number of hours a month above which the monthly plan becomes cheaper than paying by the hour.

| Provider | Configuration | Hourly | Monthly | Break-even hours | Monthly saving | Included traffic |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hetzner | GEX131 — 1x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q, 96 GB | EUR 1.4247 | EUR 889 | 624 (85%) | 14.5% | Not stated in announcement |
| Cherry Servers | 1x A40, 48 GB (pre-order) | $0.801 | $472.66 | 590 (81%) | 19.2% | 30–100 TB |
| Cherry Servers | 1x A100, 80 GB (pre-order) | $2.362 | $1,657.68 | 702 (96%) | 3.9% | 30–100 TB |
| Latitude.sh | 1x H100 80 GB, bare metal | $1.68 | $1,230 | 732 (over 100%) | none (−0.3%) | 20 TB out, inbound unmetered |
| Latitude.sh | 8x RTX PRO 6000, bare metal | $24.00 | $17,520 | 730 (100%) | none | 20 TB out |
| Latitude.sh | 8x HGX B300, bare metal | $64.00 | $46,720 | 730 (100%) | none | 20 TB out |
| OVHcloud | HGR-AI-2 — L40S | not published | from $4,355 + $4,355 installation | — | — | not stated |
| Atlantic.Net | 1x H100 NVL, managed, 12-month term | not published | $4,729.44 | — | — | 10 TB |

Sources: Hetzner pressroom (GEX131), Cherry Servers dedicated GPU servers page, Latitude.sh pricing, OVHcloud GPU dedicated server page, Atlantic.Net dedicated GPU hosting. Only the Hetzner announcement carries a date.

...

The commitment discount narrows as the hardware gets more in demand. About 19% on an A40, 14.5% on Hetzner’s workstation-class RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q, about 4% on an A100, and nothing on Latitude.sh’s H100, RTX PRO 6000 and B300 nodes. It is not a clean rule — Hetzner still discounts a

...

Lambda shows the same shape on a different product line. Its on-demand NVIDIA B200 SXM6 instance is $6.69/GPU/hr. Its 1-Click Clusters on HGX B200, sold on commitments of two weeks to one year, are $9.86/GPU/hr at 16 GPUs, $9.36 at 64 and $8.87 at 256+ — 33–47% above the on-demand rate (Lambda pricing page, checked 7 October 2026). These are different products: a cluster is interconnected multi-node capacity, an instance is a single server. Lambda reserves its “lowest prices” for terms over a year, which go through sales. The published commitment price, in other words, buys guaranteed interconnected capacity — not a discount.

...

Hetzner reprices on change, not on renewal. “For orders placed before 15 June 2026, but delivered after 15 June 2026, the previous prices will apply,” and “certain changes to servers with legacy pricing may trigger a switch to the current pricing.” Your cheapest server is your oldest one, and a consolidation that touches it can move that capacity onto current rates. Model fleet changes at today’s prices.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's $5.98 marketplace rate and just below RunPod Secure's $7.99. Its H100 at $4.59 would remain above the board's best H100 SXM offer (TensorDock, from $2.25 at an 8-GPU minimum) but move Lambda from the middle of the H100 pack toward its top. Around-the-clock, the announced rises add about $730 a month per B200, $438 per H100 and $292 per A100 80GB on a 730-hour month.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Index, November 2026: H100 to B300
highlights:
## Method

- One on-demand price per provider and GPU, taken from public pricing pages or price APIs. Prices for 8-GPU nodes are divided by eight.
- Specialist GPU clouds only for the median. Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle) are listed separately because their prices are 2.5 to 4.5 times higher.
- Monthly cost = hourly price × 730 hours. Prices exclude taxes.

## Median prices by GPU

| GPU | Prices found | Lowest $/h | Median $/h | Median / month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA B300 | 8 | 6.60 | 8.98 | $6,552 |
| NVIDIA B200 | 11 | 5.43 | 8.19 | $5,979 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 12 | 2.90 | 4.94 | $3,606 |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | 16 | 1.99 | 3.72 | $2,716 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 9 | 1.40 | 2.19 | $1,599 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 11 | 0.73 | 1.57 | $1,146 |
| AMD MI325X | 2 | 3.80 | 4.21 | $3,071 |
| AMD MI300X | 4 | 2.59 | 3.22 | $2,351 |

...

On-demand prices per GPU-hour at the largest clouds remain far above specialist clouds: H100 from $6.88 (8-GPU instance divided by eight) to more than $12 depending on the provider, and B300 from $15 to $17.80. Commitments of one to three years cut those prices by 30 to 56%.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.

results.title: RunPod Secure Cloud GPU Rates Rise: H100 $3.99, B200 $7.99
results.author: TSN Newsroom
highlights:
RunPod Secure Cloud GPU Rates Rise: H100 $3.99, B200 $7.99

# RunPod’s Secure Cloud GPU Rates Have Risen: H100 SXM Now $3.99 an Hour, B200 $7.99, a Tracker Reports

October 10, 2026

Illustration.

A GPU price tracker, GPU Economy, says RunPod raised 12 of its 29 on-demand Secure Cloud GPU rates on 8 October 2026 [1]. RunPod’s pricing page now shows the higher prices [2]. RunPod made no announcement that we could find, so the timing and the old prices rest on the tracker.

## The new rates

RunPod sells two tiers, Secure Cloud and Community Cloud; on its listings the Community rates are lower. Prices are in US dollars per GPU per hour, on demand, meaning pay as you go. GPU Economy reports [1]:

| GPU | Before | Now | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $3.49 | $3.99 | +14.3% |
| H200 | $4.59 | $5.29 | +15.3% |
| B200 | $6.79 | $7.99 | +17.7% |
| B300 | $7.89 | $8.99 | +13.9% |

The H100, H200, B200 and B300 are Nvidia data-centre chips used to train and run AI models. The tracker says the 12 rises came “between our reads of October 8, 2026 at 15:41 and 16:41 UTC”, which is 16:41 and 17:41 in London. It also computes that one H100 SXM running for a 730-hour month went from $2,547.70 to $2,912.70.

## What did not change

The tracker says “None of the 35 Community Cloud on-demand rates changed in the same read”: the H100 SXM there stayed at $2.69 and the B200 at $5.98 [1].

## What RunPod’s page shows

RunPod’s pricing page lists $3.99/hr for the H100 SXM, $7.99/hr for the B200, $5.29/hr for the H200 and $8.99/hr for the B300 [2]. But the page is labelled “Updated September 27, 2026”, which does not match the tracker’s 8 October timing. The page’s hidden structured data, the code search engines read, still lists the old Secure Cloud prices, such as $3.49 for the H100 SXM [2]. The tracker says it read RunPod’s public API, and that on 9 October the page’s own markup still carried $3.49 [1]. That fits what we see.

## What this does not show

- A RunPod announcement. We found none, and no reason for the rises.
- When RunPod made the change. The tracker reads hourly and gives a one-hour window.
- Other providers’ prices. This covers RunPod only.
- Every region or product. Serverless and cluster pricing are not covered.
